headline: Host DNA reduction and integrated metagenomic readouts refine microbiome profiling
label: Microbiome Sequence Analysis Tools
summary: Metagenomic methods now reduce host background and link microbial function to host and environmental readouts across diverse sample types.
synthesis: The dominant thread is methodological refinement of microbiome sequence analysis, applied to host-associated and environmental samples. In cattle gastrointestinal epithelium, Dilute-MetaSeq reduces host DNA interference 52.4-fold, enabling an atlas of 1,907 prokaryotic and 5,603 viral genomes. A colorectal cancer preprint combines metabolic modeling with host transcriptomes, reporting faster Fusobacterium growth in tumor microbiomes and linking microbial metabolism to tumor gene expression. PlasticEnz integrates HMM/DIAMOND homology search with ProtBERT-based classifiers to screen metagenomes for plastic-degrading enzymes, reporting F1 > 0.7. The groundwater study examines viral roles in energy-limited communities. Taken together, host-associated work is moving toward reducing host background while adding microbial-host functional readouts; the groundwater and PlasticEnz items address different questions.
